newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog says use of Blair photo in beer ad OK.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog says use of Blair photo in beer ad OK.

text.p: A British advertising watchdog group on Wednesday said a beer advertisement showing a photo of Cherie Blair, the wife of British Prime Minister Tony Blair, appearing to drink a bottle of beer did not breach advertising codes.

The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) in its monthly report said the advert was a one-off and would not generally be seen as an endorsement by the Blairs for Holsten Pils beer. The ad, created by agency GGT, featured a photo of the Blairs that had been retouched so that Mrs. Blair appeared to be raising a bottle of Holsten Pils to her lips.
The quote "All change then darling" appeared over Mr. Blair's photo. A quote over Mrs. Blair's photo read, "Yes dear, smoother, cleaner and surprisingly easy to drink."
The ASA, the ad industry's self-regulatory body for print advertisements, said it concluded the ad "...would be interpreted as humourous."

The ASA did uphold complaints against two separate car ads that emphasised speed. A poster ad for the Audi Cabriolet created by Bartle, Bogle, Hegarty which read "0 to 60 mph in 9.3 seconds" did not mention safety or careful driving and "clearly breached the codes," the ASA said. It noted that the ad is no longer running but asked the advertisers to be more responsible in the future.

The ASA also upheld complaints against an ad for the Volvo S70 T-5 that showed a stopwatch, a rocket, a sprinter and a fireball behind the car. The ad read, "Overtaking is a simple undertaking ... simply put your foot down. Keep it there and you can take the S70 T-5 all the way up to 152 mph -- should you find yourself on an authobahn, of course."
The ASA said it asked that the ad be withdrawn, noting that it emphasised speed and performance.

Earlier this month the Independent Television Commission, which oversees television advertising, upheld complaints against three separate TV adverts for cars, noting that car ads must not condone irresponsible driving.

The ASA in its August report also said it did not uphold complaints against press adverts for Lambert & Butler cigarettes. Complainants had objected to the dialogue in the ad, saying the humour was likely to appeal to children.

But the ASA said the ad, created by Mustoe Merriman Herring Levy for Imperial Tobacco, was not likely to have particular appeal to youths. The ASA did urge the advertiser to "avoid creating 'cult' figures who could appeal to young people."
